reproduction_target: De novo genome assembly and annotation pipeline for tetraploid Carya glabra: read QC (SeqKit2, fastp), organellar genome assembly and annotation (Oatk, Bandage, GeSeq, MAFFT/Geneious, BLAST vs PlantRNA 2.0, PMGA, Captus, OGDRAW), nuclear genome profiling (Jellyfish, GenomeScope 2.0), nuclear assembly and Hi-C/Omni-C scaffolding (hifiasm, bwa-mem2, hic_qc, YaHS, Juicer, Juicebox manual curation, D-GENIES, chromosome assignment, BUSCO), nuclear annotation (EDTA, RepeatMasker, BRAKER3, AGAT, TRAPID 2.0, Circos), and comparative analyses (GENESPACE, DRAGO 2/PRGdb 3.0, MCScan/JCVI). All tissue collection, DNA/RNA extraction, PacBio HiFi / Omni-C / RNA-seq library construction and sequencing are out of computational-reproduction scope (counted in W).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis derived from the 'Materials & Methods' subsections: Sample collection; DNA isolation and sequencing; RNA isolation and sequencing; Chloroplast and mitochondrial genome assembly and annotation; Nuclear genome profiling; Nuclear genome assembly; Nuclear genome annotation; Comparative genomic analyses; Identification of putative disease resistance genes. Three irreducibly manual/interactive operations are kept as their own steps because they are load-bearing for the published result and have no scripted counterpart (C4 Bandage graph editing, C10 organellar annotation-track reconciliation in Geneious Prime, C19 Juicebox Assembly Tools misjoin/inversion curation). Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted. Stage-1 prose-only: the GitLab repository landing page and the README prose were read; no script file contents were read.

steps.label: Basic statistics of PacBio HiFi, Omni-C and RNA-seq reads with SeqKit2 (v.2.4.0; Shen et al. 2024)
Filtering of raw RNA-seq reads with fastp (v.0.23.4; Chen et al. 2018) 'with default parameters'
Simultaneous chloroplast + mitochondrial genome assembly from PacBio HiFi reads with Oatk (v1.0; Zhou et al. 2025)

Manual simplification and circularization of the Oatk plastome assembly graph in Bandage (v.0.8.1; Wick et al. 2015), and manual inference of two circular mitochondrial contigs from the unresolvable mitochondrial graph ('two circular contigs were inferred from the graph and saved as separate chromosomes using Bandage')
Chloroplast genome annotation with the GeSeq web application (https://chlorobox.mpimp-golm.mpg.de/geseq.html; Tillich et al. 2017)

Alignment of the new plastome against Nicotiana tabacum NC_001879 and three published Carya glabra plastomes (BK061156, OR099205, NC_067504) using MAFFT (v.7.490) with default parameters inside Geneious Prime (2025.2.2)
Validation of ambiguous tRNA annotations by BLAST searches against the PlantRNA 2.0 database (http://plantrna.ibmp.cnrs.fr/; Cognat et al. 2022)
Annotation of the two mitochondrial chromosomes with the PMGA web application (http://47.96.249.172:16084/annotate.html; Li et al. 2025) 'using the three databases available in the program'
Search for plastome and mitochondrial proteins with Captus (v.1.6.1; Ortiz et al. 2023) to produce a fourth annotation track

Manual reconciliation of four organellar annotation tracks (one Captus + three PMGA) 'retaining only the best annotation (i.e., that includes start and stop codons whenever possible, longest and/or most frequently observed) in case of discrepancies', plus manual inspection/curation of the plastome annotation and export of edited GenBank files from Geneious Prime
Generation of chloroplast and mitochondrial annotation maps with OGDRAW (v.1.3.1; Greiner et al. 2019) using default parameters except checking the 'tidy up annotation' box
k-mer counting and k-mer histogram generation from HiFi reads with Jellyfish (v2.3.0; Marcais and Kingsford 2011), k-mer size 21

Nuclear genome profiling (monoploid genome size, heterozygosity, autotetraploid inference) with GenomeScope 2.0 (http://genomescope.org/genomescope2.0/; Ranallo-Benavidez et al. 2020), default parameters except ploidy set to 4

De novo nuclear assembly with hifiasm (v.0.19.9; Cheng et al. 2021) 'with default parameters', using both HiFi reads and Omni-C reads as input; the unitig assembly containing all four haplotypes was carried forward
Alignment of Omni-C reads to the unitig assembly with bwa-mem2 (v.2.2.1; Vasimuddin et al. 2019)
Omni-C library quality assessment with the hic_qc pipeline from Phase Genomics (Seattle, WA, USA); output reported as Table S6
Hi-C/Omni-C scaffolding of the unitig assembly with YaHS (v.1.1; Zhou et al. 2023) 'with default parameters'
Hi-C contact map generation with the 'juicer pre' tool from YaHS plus Juicer (v.1.22.01; Durand et al. 2016), using the Omni-C alignment file as input

Manual curation of the scaffolded assembly in Juicebox Assembly Tools (v.1.11.08; Dudchenko et al. 2018): misjoin and inversion errors manually corrected and chromosome orientation curated to match the published Carya illinoinensis genome (Lovell et al. 2021); illustrated in Fig. S2
Generation of the final chromosome-level assembly with the 'juicer post' tool from YaHS after all manual edits

Dot-plot comparison of the Carya illinoinensis genome against the assembled C. glabra genome with the D-GENIES web application (https://dgenies.toulouse.inra.fr/; Cabanettes and Klopp 2018) (Fig. 5c, Fig. S1)

Assignment of scaffolds to chromosomes and to haplotypes: scaffolds renamed according to their alignment with C. illinoinensis chromosomes; the four copies of each chromosome labelled A-D in descending order of length; naming follows Cannon et al. (2025)
Genome completeness estimation per haplotype with BUSCO (v.5.3.0; Manni et al. 2021) against the eudicots_odb10 database
De novo transposable element annotation per haplotype with EDTA (v.2.1.0; Ou et al. 2019)
Identification of additional repeat elements and soft-masking with RepeatMasker (v.4.1.7; Smit et al. 2013-2015) using the EDTA-generated TE library

Protein-coding gene prediction with BRAKER3 (v.3.0.8; Gabriel et al. 2024) using C. glabra leaf and axillary-bud RNA-seq plus protein evidence from 14 model species (Table S1); several parameter settings tested on haplotype A (Table S2) and the highest-BUSCO setting applied to haplotypes B, C, D
Filtering of gene models with AGAT (v.1.4.2; Dainat 2022): removal of models with a premature stop codon, missing start and/or stop codon, or ORF length <=100 aa or <=50 aa

Functional annotation with the TRAPID 2.0 web application (Bucchini et al. 2021) using the PLAZA 4.5 dicots database (Van Bel et al. 2018) as reference and the rosids clade for the similarity search; all parameters default except 'input sequences are CDS'
Circos (v.0.69-9; Krzywinski et al. 2009) visualization of the genome with gene, transposon, copia and gypsy densities in 100-kb sliding windows (Fig. 5a)

Genome-level synteny analysis with GENESPACE (v.1.3.1; Lovell et al. 2022) comparing the four C. glabra haplotypes with chromosome-level assemblies of C. cathayensis, C. illinoinensis and C. sinensis (Fig. 6)

Prediction of plant disease resistance genes (CNL, TNL, RLP, RLK) with the DRAGO 2 pipeline from PRGdb 3.0 (Osuna-Cruz et al. 2018) 'with default parameters', for the four C. glabra haplotypes and for C. illinoinensis, C. cathayensis and C. sinensis

Detection and visualization of C. glabra syntenic regions corresponding to the C. illinoinensis phylloxera-resistance QTL (chr16: 1,521,681-2,392,040, between CiLak.16G012100 and CiLak.16G019000) using MCScan from JCVI (v.1.2.10; Tang et al. 2024) (Fig. 7)

headline.static_readiness: 0/32 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: Readiness upper bound (RI+R*) = 21/32 (66%) at stage 1. This paper is unusually strong on the DATA axis and moderately strong on VERSION-as-prose, and weak on CODE IDENTITY and on the irreducibly manual steps. Data: raw PacBio HiFi, Omni-C and RNA-seq are under BioProject PRJNA1373287 (5 SRA runs resolve), the four haplotype assemblies under PRJNA1376128-PRJNA1376131 (resolve), and the annotation plus organellar genomes are on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.17969322, CC-BY-4.0, open, and it contains not only final GFF/FASTA but intermediate EDTA TEanno GFF3 and TRAPID export tables) - so data=2 on essentially every step. Version: 22 of 32 steps carry an exact prose pin (SeqKit2 v2.4.0, fastp v0.23.4, Oatk v1.0, Bandage v0.8.1, MAFFT v7.490, Geneious Prime 2025.2.2, Captus v1.6.1, OGDRAW v1.3.1, Jellyfish v2.3.0, hifiasm v0.19.9, bwa-mem2 v2.2.1, YaHS v1.1, Juicer v1.22.01, Juicebox v1.11.08, BUSCO v5.3.0, EDTA v2.1.0, RepeatMasker v4.1.7, BRAKER3 v3.0.8, AGAT v1.4.2, Circos v0.69-9, GENESPACE v1.3.1, JCVI v1.2.10) - but there is NO environment closure anywhere: no conda environment.yml, no lockfile, no container, no interpreter/channel/platform declaration in the paper or on the repository landing page, so version is capped at 1 (subtier exact_pins_partial) for every step by construction. Five tools/services are wholly unversioned (GeSeq, PMGA, D-GENIES, hic_qc, BLAST-vs-PlantRNA) and cap those steps at NI. The binding structural constraint, however, is CODE IDENTITY plus MANUAL CURATION: the paper says 'All codes and scripts are available at: https://gitlab.com/shengchenshan/bot4935-plant-genome-assembly-and-annotation', the repo is live and public with stage-named directories (01-input, 02-quality_control, 03-organelle_genomes, 04-nuclear_assembly, 05-structural_annotation, 07-comparative_analysis, plus Useful.command.lines.md and Data_submission_workflow.md), but it has 0 tags, 0 releases, no Zenodo archive of the code, a floating main branch whose last activity (2026-05-22) postdates the preprint, and a README that is still the unedited default GitLab template (93 lines of 'Add your files' / 'Choose a self-explaining name for your project') - it names not one script and even still points at a different course repo (bsc2930-...). So at Stage-1 prose level no step can be scored code=2 (public+exact); every scripted step is code=1 (reconstructable). Three steps are unrecoverable regardless of code: C4 (Bandage manual graph simplification and manual inference of the two mitochondrial chromosomes), C10 (manual reconciliation of four organellar annotation tracks by a subjective 'best annotation' rule in commercial Geneious Prime), C19 (Juicebox manual misjoin/inversion correction - Fig. S2 shows it happened, but no .assembly/review file is deposited). Those three are X and no amount of Stage-2 code reading can rescue them; only depositing the curation records would. A Stage-2 code check could raise many code=1 to code=2, but under rubric Delta-2 the version axis still caps at 1 with no env lock, so R-star would remain 0 - which is why stage2_candidate is false.
headline.coverage: 32 computational steps assessed from the 'Materials & Methods' prose. 7 wet-lab steps counted (W, out of computational-reproduction scope): tissue collection and herbarium voucher deposition; HMW DNA extraction (Nanobind Plant Nuclei Big DNA Kit), Megaruptor shearing and BluePippin ~25 kb size selection with SMRTbell Express Template Prep Kit 2.0; PacBio Revio HiFi sequencing on two SMRT cells; Omni-C library construction by the Dovetail Genomics protocol; Illumina NovaSeq 6000 S4 paired-end 150 bp sequencing of the Omni-C library; RNA extraction by modified CTAB (Jordon-Thaden et al. 2015) with Bioanalyzer RIN QC; strand-specific RNA-seq library preparation and Illumina NovaSeq X paired-end 151 bp sequencing. Computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 32/39 = 82%. Both a 'Data availability' statement and a code pointer are present; there is no separately headed 'Code availability' section - the code sentence sits inside 'Data availability' and is repeated in the education paragraph of the Discussion.

gaps.where: Software environment for the entire pipeline (all 32 C-steps)
gaps.missing: No environment capture of any kind is claimed in the paper or visible on the repository landing page: no conda environment.yml, no conda-lock/pixi.lock, no Dockerfile or container digest, no Singularity definition, no requirements.txt, no renv.lock. The top-level GitLab tree contains only stage directories plus README.md, Useful.command.lines.md and Data_submission_workflow.md. No interpreter versions (Perl for Circos/RepeatMasker/EDTA, Python for JCVI, R for GENESPACE) and no channels/platform are declared anywhere. Computation ran on the University of Florida HiPerGator cluster, so an environment-module stack is implied but never enumerated. Version therefore caps at 1 (exact_pins_partial) for every step even though 22 of 32 tools carry an exact prose pin.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock / pixi.lock / container digest covering the assembly and annotation stack (hifiasm, YaHS, Juicer, BUSCO, EDTA, RepeatMasker, BRAKER3 with its AUGUSTUS/GeneMark-ETP/TSEBRA components, AGAT, GENESPACE with OrthoFinder/DIAMOND/MCScanX, JCVI, Circos) plus the declared platform, and record the HiPerGator module versions actually loaded.

gaps.where: C5 GeSeq, C7 BLAST vs PlantRNA 2.0, C8 PMGA, C16 hic_qc, C21 D-GENIES
gaps.missing: Five tools are cited with no version at all: the GeSeq web application, the BLAST program used against PlantRNA 2.0 (program flavour also unstated), the PMGA web application, the Phase Genomics hic_qc pipeline (cited without URL, version or reference), and the D-GENIES web application. These five steps are capped at version=0 and hence at NI.
gaps.how_to_close: State the release/date of each web service used and the version of hic_qc and BLAST+, or record the run identifiers/permalinks the services issue.

gaps.missing: The code is cited as a bare floating URL. The project has 0 tags and 0 releases, no Zenodo DOI for the code (the two Zenodo DOIs cited are for lecture slides 10.5281/zenodo.17969442 and for the annotation/organellar data 10.5281/zenodo.17969322 - neither archives the code), and the default branch main is mutable with last_activity_at 2026-05-22, i.e. after the 2025-12-23 preprint. The repository has 24 forks, so divergent copies already exist. There is no commit SHA anywhere in the paper, so the exact code state behind the published assembly cannot be recovered.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a release corresponding to the preprint, archive it to Zenodo for a DOI, and cite that DOI (or at minimum the commit SHA) in the Data availability statement.

gaps.where: Mapping from Methods steps to repository scripts (all 32 C-steps)
gaps.missing: The repository README is still the unedited default GitLab template (93 lines of 'Add your files', 'Integrate with your tools', 'Editing this README'); it names no script, documents no run order, states no inputs/outputs, gives no license and no requirements, and the boilerplate clone URL it contains still points to a different course repository (bsc2930-plant-genome-assembly-and-annotation). The landing page therefore provides no prose evidence that any particular Methods step corresponds to a particular file; only the six stage-named directories suggest coverage, and there is no directory numbered 06, so functional annotation (TRAPID) appears to have no directory. The paper's claim 'All codes and scripts are available' cannot be checked at Stage 1.
gaps.how_to_close: Replace the template README with a real one: per-stage run order, the exact command lines for each Methods step, inputs/outputs, the compute environment, and a license. Add a table mapping each Methods subsection and each figure to the script that produces it.

gaps.where: C4 Bandage graph editing, C10 organellar annotation-track reconciliation, C19 Juicebox Assembly Tools curation, C22 chromosome/haplotype assignment
gaps.missing: Four load-bearing operations are manual and leave no deposited record. C4: the plastome graph was 'simplified and circularized' by hand and 'two circular contigs were inferred from the graph' for the mitogenome after excluding graph segments - which segments were excluded, and on what criterion, is not stated. C10: where the four annotation tracks disagreed, the 'best' one was kept by a subjective rule ('includes start and stop codons whenever possible, longest and/or most frequently observed'); the curation was done in commercial Geneious Prime and only the final GenBank was exported. C19: 'Misjoin and inversion errors were manually corrected' in Juicebox - Fig. S2 shows the curation, but the Juicebox .assembly / review file that encodes the edits is not in the Zenodo deposit or the repository, so 'juicer post' (C20) cannot be re-run. C22: scaffold renaming by alignment to C. illinoinensis is described as a rule, but the alignment tool/thresholds used for the assignment and the tie-break for equal-length haplotype copies are unstated.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the Juicebox review/.assembly file and the pre-curation YaHS scaffolds, the Bandage graph files (GFA before/after) with the list of excluded segments, and the four raw organellar annotation tracks plus the reconciliation decisions; script the chromosome-assignment step.

gaps.where: C5 GeSeq, C8 PMGA, C13 GenomeScope 2.0, C21 D-GENIES, C28 TRAPID 2.0, C31 DRAGO 2/PRGdb 3.0, C11 OGDRAW
gaps.missing: Seven analysis steps are externalized to web applications with no local execution path and no exported run configuration. Two of them (PMGA at the bare IP endpoint http://47.96.249.172:16084/annotate.html, and the DRAGO 2 service at PRGdb) are single-point-of-failure endpoints whose availability and backend version are outside author control. TRAPID experiment identifiers (exp7998-exp8002) are visible in the deposited output filenames, which is helpful, but no TRAPID job export or session link is cited in the paper.
gaps.how_to_close: Where a command-line equivalent exists (e.g. a local annotation pipeline instead of GeSeq/PMGA, a local GenomeScope R script, a local DIAMOND/HMMER R-gene pipeline), run and ship it alongside; otherwise cite the service run identifiers and archive both the service inputs and the raw service outputs.

gaps.where: C6 MAFFT-inside-Geneious and C10 organellar curation/export
gaps.missing: Geneious Prime 2025.2.2 is a commercial, licence-gated application. The plastome alignment and the whole organellar annotation curation and GenBank export were performed inside it. The version is pinned, which is the best case for a proprietary dependency, but a reader without a Geneious licence cannot re-execute these steps, so they are ceiling-capped at NI (C6) and X (C10, which is additionally manual).
gaps.how_to_close: Run the alignment with standalone MAFFT v7.490 and ship the command line and the alignment file; export the curation as a scripted GFF/GenBank diff rather than as a Geneious project.

gaps.where: C7 PlantRNA 2.0, C23 BUSCO eudicots_odb10, C25 RepeatMasker repeat library, C28 PLAZA 4.5 dicots, C31 PRGdb 3.0, C8 PMGA's three databases
gaps.missing: Reference databases are named but not pinned to a release/date/checksum: the eudicots_odb10 dataset release date is unstated (BUSCO re-downloads the current copy), the RepeatMasker Dfam/RepBase library release backing v4.1.7 is unstated, PLAZA 4.5 dicots and PRGdb 3.0 are consumed through web services whose backing snapshot can change, PlantRNA 2.0 is queried interactively, and PMGA's 'three databases available in the program' are neither named nor versioned. At Stage 1 these cannot be classified A/B/C (that is a Stage-2 code read), so env_capture_class stays n/a for every step.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the exact dataset release strings (e.g. eudicots_odb10 dated release, Dfam version) and, where possible, deposit the database snapshots or their checksums with the code.

gaps.missing: No random seed or thread count is reported for the assembly and gene-prediction steps. hifiasm graph tie-breaking and BRAKER3's self-training (GeneMark-ETP, AUGUSTUS parameter training, TSEBRA combination) are non-deterministic in practice; re-running is expected to give distributionally similar but not identical output. Additionally, the winning BRAKER3 parameter combination is only identifiable via Table S2, and the final ORF-length filter is ambiguous in the main text, which offers two thresholds ('<=100 amino acids or <=50 amino acids') while the Results say the best setting filtered at <=50 aa.
gaps.how_to_close: Report seeds and thread counts, and state the single final BRAKER3 configuration and AGAT filter threshold in the Methods rather than only in a supplementary table.

gaps.where: Sample-to-accession mapping for the deposited sequencing data
gaps.missing: The Data availability statement gives one raw-data BioProject (PRJNA1373287, which resolves and holds 5 SRA runs) and an assembly BioProject range written as 'PRJNA1376128-PRJNA1376131' with no statement of which BioProject corresponds to which haplotype (A/B/C/D). Individual SRR run accessions are not enumerated per library type (2 HiFi SMRT cells, 1 Omni-C library, 2 RNA-seq libraries), and the two RNA-seq libraries (leaf vs axillary bud) are not mapped to accessions in the text. The herbarium voucher is stated as deposited at FLAS but no voucher/catalogue number is given.
gaps.how_to_close: Tabulate library -> SRR accession -> BioSample, state the haplotype-to-BioProject correspondence explicitly, and cite the FLAS voucher barcode.

gaps.where: Wet-lab: tissue collection and voucher deposition; HMW DNA extraction, shearing, size selection and SMRTbell library construction; PacBio Revio HiFi sequencing; Omni-C library construction; Illumina NovaSeq 6000 Omni-C sequencing; CTAB RNA extraction and Bioanalyzer QC; strand-specific RNA-seq library preparation and NovaSeq X sequencing
gaps.missing: Wet-lab generation steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W (7 steps), not verdicted. Note that the modified CTAB protocol is cited (Jordon-Thaden et al. 2015) but that reference does not appear in the reference list scan, and the RNA-seq library kit is not named.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; scope is the assembly/annotation/comparative pipeline.
